name: soc_2018_titles
title: SOC 2018 job titles — direct match titles (U.S.)
description: The job titles the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics codes to each detailed occupation of the 2018 Standard Occupational Classification, for coding free-text job titles from job postings, HR extracts and survey answers: one row per title in BLS's direct match title file, with the code it points at and that code's title in bls/soc_2018. BLS marks some titles as illustrative examples of an occupation rather than direct matches, and illustrative carries the mark. Every code is a detailed occupation in bls/soc_2018, which the run checks against the code list it builds; three detailed occupations (11-9039, 19-2099 and 51-9199) have no titles in BLS's file. No title appears under two codes. BLS's files are U.S. Government works in the public domain.

entry_id.description: The entry's key, its code and title joined with '|' (11-1011|Admiral). BLS gives its titles no id of its own.

title.description: The job title as BLS's direct match title file prints it (Admiral), trimmed.

code.description: The detailed occupation BLS codes the title to, in bls/soc_2018's form (11-1011).

code_description.description: The code's title in bls/soc_2018 (Chief Executives), so a lookup needs no second join.

release.description: The release of bls/soc_2018, the code list the titles point at, as <year>/<date>: 2018/2020-04-15. BLS's direct match title file gives the same update date ("November 2017 (Updated April 15, 2020)"), and the run fails if the two files' dates differ.

text_source.description: Whose text title is: always bls, BLS's own title.

corpus.description: Lowercased, accent-stripped title, with runs of whitespace collapsed to one space: a derived free-text search field, not a source attribute.

illustrative.description: True where BLS marks the title with an x (in either case) as an illustrative example of the occupation rather than a direct match for it; false for a direct match.
